$comment: The angle vocabulary. The model picks three of these, one per game, and may use no other label. Criterion 6. A free-text 'reason' field would give a gate that passes on 'atmospheric', 'very atmospheric' and 'atmosphere-focused', which is why this is a fixed list checked by membership.
howChecked: Each angle is either constrained or judgement. A constrained angle names a condition code can test against catalogue data, so the model calling a singleplayer game 'the one to play with someone' is caught. A judgement angle names nothing checkable and code only verifies the label is in this list and does not repeat. Which is which is written down rather than left implicit, because a gate whose reach is unclear gets trusted further than it earns.
warning: Constrained angles inherit pitfall 18. Tags fail in both directions: a genuinely co-operative game that RAWG has not tagged will be rejected, the same way Hades is not tagged difficult. Every rejection is logged with the reason so the false-rejection rate is measurable rather than assumed.

angles.label: the safe pick
angles.meaning: The most squarely what they asked for. If they only play one, this one.

angles.label: the deep cut
angles.meaning: Less known than the others, same appeal. The one they probably have not heard of.

angles.label: the beautiful one
angles.meaning: Worth playing for how it looks and sounds alone.

angles.label: the one to play with someone
angles.meaning: Playable with another person, in the same room or online.

angles.label: the hard one
angles.meaning: The one that will actually fight back.

angles.label: the short one
angles.meaning: Finishable in an evening or two, for someone without sixty hours.

constraint.$comment: RAWG reports playtime in hours and it is frequently 0, meaning unknown rather than instant. A candidate with playtime 0 fails this constraint rather than passing it — an unknown length is not evidence of a short game. See src/shortlist.js.
